findings.title: epoll EFAULT loses edge-triggered readiness
findings.summary: EpollFile::wait removes an edge-triggered ready entry before sys_epoll_wait copies it to user memory. If that copy faults, the syscall returns EFAULT but the ready edge is not restored, so a later valid epoll_wait sees no event. The bounded model reaches the lost-undelivered epoch in nine states and the public eventfd reproduction observes the missing redelivery in an SMP=2 Asterinas VM.

findings.title: epoll EFAULT disables one-shot interest before delivery
findings.summary: Entry::poll disables an EPOLLONESHOT observer when it observes readiness, before the selected event is copied to user memory. A copyout EFAULT therefore leaves an event that was never delivered permanently disabled until EPOLL_CTL_MOD. The ten-state model trace and the SMP=2 public eventfd test both show this behavior.

findings.title: final close leaves a dead epoll interest entry
findings.summary: The epoll key includes the weak file-object identity, preventing descriptor-number reuse from retargeting a watch, but final close has no immediate epoll cleanup hook. The dead weak entry remains in the interest set until a later ready-list scan notices it. The seven-state model trace is directly observable through a stale /proc/self/fdinfo entry in the SMP=2 VM test.

findings.title: consumed timerfd remains ready through the poll cache
findings.summary: Timerfd expiration invalidates and caches readiness, but a successful read clears ticks without invalidating the shared Pollee cache. A subsequent zero-timeout poll can report POLLIN even though the next read returns EAGAIN. The nine-state model trace and public timerfd reproduction both show stale readiness.

findings.title: signalfd mask update does not publish readiness
findings.summary: Updating an existing signalfd mask only stores the new mask. A signal that was already pending can become readable under that new mask without notifying the thread or process signal-queue poller registered by epoll. The temporal counterexample reaches the lost transition in eight states and the SMP=2 signalfd test times out instead of receiving the pending signal.

findings.title: poll returns timeout after timerfd becomes readable
findings.summary: The timeout return path in do_poll does not rescan descriptors after the waiting primitive returns ETIME. A timerfd can increment its readable tick counter at the timeout boundary, yet poll returns zero; an immediate read then succeeds. The six-state model trace is reproduced in repeated SMP=2 timerfd stress runs.
